title: Why twins with the same birth chart live different lives | Ask Tota
description: Twins born minutes apart share almost every planet. How much their charts differ, what Vedic astrology says about it, and what the research on time twins found.
og_title: Twins, birth charts and different lives
og_description: Same parents, same sky, a few minutes apart. Where twin charts really differ, how the tradition explains it, and what science says.
h1: twins share a sky but not a chart. here is where the minutes go
dek: the twins question is the oldest objection to astrology, and jyotish has been answering it for centuries. a few minutes barely move the planets but can shift the divisional charts, the lagna degree and the dasha dates. here is exactly how much differs, and what the research found.

faq.q: do twins have the same birth chart?
faq.a: nearly. twins born minutes apart share the same planets in the same signs and usually the same lagna sign. what differs is the exact lagna degree, the divisional charts, and slightly the dasha dates. how much depends on how far apart they were born.

faq.q: why do twins have different lives if their charts are the same?
faq.a: vedic astrology points to differences in the fine divisional charts and dasha timing. beyond astrology, twins differ in genes (if fraternal), experiences, choices and relationships. research on time twins found no extra similarity from shared charts.

faq.q: how much does a few minutes change a birth chart?
faq.a: the lagna moves about a degree every four minutes. the planets barely move: even the moon shifts only about one degree every two hours. so the d1 chart is usually identical, while the d9 lagna can change about every 13 minutes and the d60 every 2.

faq.q: can two people have the same birth chart?
faq.a: two people born at the same minute in the same place have the same chart. this happens constantly across a large population. those time twins do not lead identical lives, which is one of the most cited observations about astrology.

faq.q: what does vedic astrology say about twins?
faq.a: traditional astrologers use the divisional charts, especially the d60 shashtiamsa, and sometimes treat the second twin as reading from a rotated chart. these methods exist precisely because the d1 alone does not separate twins.

faq.q: what is the d60 chart and why does it matter for twins?
faq.a: the shashtiamsa divides each sign into 60 parts of half a degree. its lagna changes about every two minutes, so twins born a few minutes apart often have different d60 charts. parashara gives the d60 great weight.

faq.q: what did the time twins study find?
faq.a: geoffrey dean and ivan kelly followed 2,101 people born in london in march 1958 and compared those born close together on over 100 traits. they found no more similarity than between random pairs.

faq.q: do twins have the same dasha?
faq.a: the same dasha sequence and almost the same dates. the moon moves only about half a degree an hour, so a few minutes changes dasha dates by days or weeks, not years.

faq.q: do twins born on different days have different charts?
faq.a: yes. twins born either side of midnight can have a different moon nakshatra and sometimes a different moon sign, which changes their dasha timeline significantly.

faq.q: are identical twins a problem for astrology?
faq.a: they are one of the strongest tests of it, because they share genes, parents, upbringing and nearly the same chart, yet live distinct lives. astrology answers through fine divisional charts; critics argue this shows the chart is not the deciding factor.

faq.q: which twin is older in astrology?
faq.a: the one born first, with the earlier birth time. their charts are calculated separately from their exact times, so it matters to record both births to the minute.
yes, with their individual birth times recorded as precisely as possible. a reading that uses the same chart for both is skipping the part where twins actually differ.
